subject: Intermittent SYN retries during staging cutover - handoff corridor triage
messages:
From: SRE - DataGrid <sre@datagrid.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [DataGrid] Staging cutover: spikes of SYN retries / silent drops

Hi Karthik,

We cut the staging-to-production northbound handoff at 03:40 PT and started seeing a pattern of short-lived SYN retries for downstream API traffic to your private edge. Symptoms: 2-3 second bursts where ~0.5% requests show repeated SYNs then succeed after 10-20s, and a correlated spike in connection resets on our side. We've captured a sample pcap and a short nat translation dump (attached).

What we observed in the pcap: a cluster of SYNs with MSS=1460, many metrics show DF set, and a handful of SYNs appear to disappear between our egress hop and Redwood's ingress (we see no RST from your side). Translation logs show transient new NAT entries with port re-use and short-lived translations.

This is causing aborted test runs and blocks our performance tests. Can you confirm whether anything changed in the private handoff (SNAT behavior, port allocation, MTU/clamping, or ECN marking) around the cutover window? Also attaching traces and the pcap.

Attachments: pcap-datagrid-staging-20261122.zip (pcap), nat-translation-sample.log (text)

Thanks,
Alex Kim
SRE — DataGrid
ops@datagrid.io

Subject: Re: [DataGrid] Staging cutover: spikes of SYN retries / silent drops

Alex — thanks for the report and the pcap. We're pulling a small triage group together. Quick notes from an initial look:

- I see the same SYN bursts in the pcap. Most SYNs carry DF and MSS=1460. No explicit RSTs from our side.
- The translation log shows rapid ephemeral port reuse; some ports are reallocated <1s after close in the timeframe you captured. That can surface as apparent "silent" retries when a new client rebinds to an in-use tuple.
- Vanessa mentioned a kernel patch rollout — we'll treat that as a potential trigger.

Immediate asks: can you confirm whether our edge hosts that received the kernel patch are in the path for the failed flows (we'll correlate your source IPs with our routing map)? Also please share any BGP/route change logs if any were run in the same window.

I'll coordinate an action plan below and propose a short mitigation: enable our NAT port-preserving fallback and increase conntrack ephemeral port window on the affected NAT hosts while we root cause. Rishi, can you prepare the config snippet and rollback notes? Marissa, please keep DataGrid in the loop for any short maintenance we need to run.

-Karthik
Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: [DataGrid] Staging cutover: spikes of SYN retries / silent drops

Adding telemetry details from the edge hosts that received the kernel patch:

- Kernel bump changed the default nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established from 5d to 2d on the patched image (we patched the image to align with our new scaling profile).
- conntrack_slab/alloc metrics show no immediate exhaustion but there are short bursts of NAT table churn around the cutover window (matches their timestamps).
- MTU: we have not changed PMTU or clamping rules — still default 1500 across the transit. However, I do see a handful of ECN-marked frames originating from a transit peer at 03:41 PT in their flow trace (we can include that if needed).

Hypothesis: the kernel change reduced established-timeout making ephemeral re-use occur faster under certain client connection patterns. Combined with port reallocation on high churn flows, this surfaces as transient SYN retries. If ECN marking coincides, it could exacerbate retransmit behavior on some stacks.

I'm attaching a short translation example and a query I ran against the conntrack dump. Rishi — if you can validate port allocation policy and craft the fallback config, that'd be great.

- Vanessa
Sr. Network Engineer — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: nat-translation-sample.log (text)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE - DataGrid <sre@datagrid.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [DataGrid] Staging cutover: spikes of SYN retries / silent drops

All — I prepared a short mitigation and rollback plan. Applied to the NAT farm in canary (2 hosts) at 12:40 PT and observed the following in the next 10 minutes: outbound SYN retries from their test range dropped to zero in our telemetry window.

Mitigation applied (canary):
- Enabled port-preserving fallback on the NAT module (keeps source port where possible until confirmed conflict).
- Increased ephemeral port range: 32768-61000 -> 32768-64000 to reduce re-use pressure.
- Tuned conntrack tcp timeouts: tcp_close_wait=60, tcp_fin_timeout=30, tcp_tw_timeout shortened to 30.

Rollback notes: each change is reversible via profile rollback. The port-preserving toggle has no impact on established flows and is safe for short windows; ephemeral range increase is additive. Full rollback command set in the playbook attached.

Playbook (attached): redwood-playbook-nat-fallback.md — includes exact commands, verification queries, and dashboards to watch (conntrack_nat_events, nat_port_realloc_rate).

Next steps: 1) extend to full NAT pool after DataGrid validates, 2) have EquiNet validate that no middlebox OS changes interact poorly with port-preserving behaviour, 3) schedule a follow-up postmortem to correlate kernel patch with the artifact.

-Rishi
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-playbook-nat-fallback.md (doc)

Subject: Re: [DataGrid] Staging cutover: spikes of SYN retries / silent drops

Karthik / Rishi — quick update from our side after your canary change: the test harness completed three runs with zero SYN retry spikes. We applied the canary to our staging egress path and observed the same positive result.

We do still see two very small anomalies: occasional ECN-marked packets followed by one RTT delay on a tiny subset of flows (0.02%). That looks like forced ECN/CE from a transit peer, and we will open a ticket with them. For now the primary pain (SYN retries / aborted tests) is resolved by your NAT fallback.

Next asks: can Redwood run a directed MTU+DF test from the affected edge cluster to our test range (we've attached a second pcap from a post-mitigation run). We want to confirm there's no blackhole when DF=1 and a 1500->1460 path for some peers. Also, please include the proof of rollback steps we can call if the mitigation causes side effects.

Thanks for the rapid turn. We can keep the mitigation in place until the postmortem.

— Alex Kim
SRE — DataGrid
